name: Panel
description: A lightweight bordered surface with optional header and actions, for grouping content without Card's elevation.

anatomy.description: The title-plus-actions row, rendered only when title or actions are provided.
The heading naming the grouped content, adjustable to fit the page outline.
The trailing slot for one small related control.
The bordered content region without Card's elevation.

dos: Use it for quiet grouping like settings blocks and summaries.
Keep header actions to a single small control.
Choose Panel over Card when elevation would add noise.
donts: Don't make the panel itself clickable; put a real link or button inside.
Don't nest panels inside panels; flatten the grouping instead.

examples.title: Panel with header and actions
examples.description: A titled panel with a trailing action, the default way to frame a self-contained block of content.

examples.title: Headerless and action-only panels
examples.description: Omit the title for a simple bordered group, or pass actions alone when the content speaks for itself.

guidance.useWhen: You need to group related content on the page with a light boundary, for example settings blocks, summaries, or sidebar sections.
guidance.avoidWhen: The surface is a primary, clickable, or elevated content unit; use Card instead, which carries stronger elevation and an interactive variant.
guidance.behavior: Panel is a static container: it renders a header row only when a title or actions are provided and adds no interaction of its own.
guidance.responsive: The header row keeps its items on one line with a gap and relies on the flexible width of the panel, so it fills narrow columns without extra work.

notes: The title renders a real heading (h2 by default, adjustable via titleAs), so screen-reader users can navigate between panels.
Actions are plain interactive elements and keep their own accessible names and focus rings.
